plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bidding your true value minus a small amount to increase the chance of winning while still ensuring a positive profit. However, in a single round, and with a high value of $19, a slightly more aggressive approach is warranted. Since all bidders are rational, and values are between $0 and $20, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the second highest bid. In a symmetric equilibrium, each player bids (2/3)*value. However, my value is $24, which is outside the possible range. I should bid my true value, as any lower bid risks losing the auction to someone with a lower value, and any higher bid risks overpaying.

Since all bidders are rational and know each other are rational, a dominant strategy emerges: bid your true value. This is because any lower bid risks losing the auction when your value exceeds the second-highest bid, resulting in lost potential profit. Bidding higher than your value guarantees a loss, as you'll pay more than the item is worth to you. My value is $21, so I bid $21.
